title: Why People Believe in Conspiracy Theories | Psychology Explained
description:
From the moon landing hoax to flat earth societies, from vaccines cause autism to COVID-19 as biological warfare, conspiracy theories thrive in the age of social media. But why do so many people fall for them?

In this documentary, Pale Blue Thoughts explores the psychology and science behind conspiracy theories. Humans are natural pattern seekers, finding meaning where none exists — from seeing faces in clouds to connecting random events. Add the need to belong to a group, narcissism (“I’m smarter than the rest”), and distrust of authority, and you get fertile ground for conspiracies.

We examine popular conspiracies:

Moon landing hoax

Flat earth claims

Climate change denial

Vaccines causing autism

9/11 “inside job” theories

Aliens building pyramids

COVID-19 as a lab-made bioweapon

conspiracy theories

To cut through the noise, we dive into David Robert Grimes’s 2016 PLOS ONE study, which used mathematics to show why large conspiracies can’t survive long. For example, with over 400,000 people working on the Apollo project, the “moon hoax” would’ve leaked within 4 years. Yet more than 50 years later, not a single whistleblower has proven it false.

This video is a call to critical thinking and scientific temper. As Brandolini’s Law reminds us, refuting nonsense takes more effort than creating it. But if we value truth, we must challenge fearmongering and misinformation.

If you’ve searched for why people believe conspiracies, conspiracy theories debunked, psychology of conspiracies, flat earth exposed, or vaccine autism myth explained, this video gives you the rational perspective.
